Bitcoin miner IREN still gets 82% of revenue from BTC after clearing room for Microsoft AI cloud
Coinbase’s $104M US500 trading spike hits an early reality check
Cosmos Labs says it wrongly cleared the bug behind a $5.7 million six-chain hack
Polygon discloses security flaws fixed in recent hard forks

en.title: Crypto Mix: Hacks, Miner Steadiness, Exchange Surge and Cross‑Chain Alert
en.body:
Over the past 24 hours, the cryptocurrency landscape has been shaped by contrasting forces: security incidents that shook confidence, steady revenue streams for Bitcoin miners, and a notable spike in futures trading on a major exchange.

A exploit targeting a crypto-card service resulted in the theft of roughly $1.1 million, causing the neobank’s AVICI token to plunge 49% from its 24‑hour high before recovering part of the loss. The incident underscores how vulnerabilities in payment‑linked products can quickly translate into sharp price moves for associated tokens. (Source: CoinDesk)

Bitcoin miner IREN reported that, even after allocating resources to support a Microsoft AI cloud initiative, roughly 82% of its revenue continues to come from $BTC holdings. The company’s $4 billion contracted AI run‑rate target remains far above current operating levels, indicating that core mining operations still dominate its earnings mix. (Source: CryptoSlate)

On the trading front, Coinbase recorded a surge of $104 million in turnover for its US500 futures product during the launch week. While the initial burst highlighted strong demand for leveraged exposure to traditional‑index products, later snapshots showed a tapering of open interest, suggesting the enthusiasm may be short‑lived. (Source: CryptoSlate)

Cosmos Labs disclosed that a patch it believed had resolved a critical vulnerability was actually issued only twenty hours before a six‑chain attack that extracted about $5.7 million. The affected networks, which include the Cosmos hub and its associated $ATOM token, claimed the fix did not address the flaw that was ultimately exploited, raising questions about the timing and efficacy of security updates in interconnected ecosystems. (Source: The Block)

Despite the security setbacks affecting payment cards and cross‑chain bridges, Bitcoin‑focused miners like IREN continue to rely on the flagship cryptocurrency for the bulk of their income, while exchange‑traded products show that traders are still willing to take on leveraged positions. The juxtaposition of exploit‑driven token declines and steady miner revenue highlights how different segments of the crypto ecosystem can react independently to the same news cycle.
